<thought>The 13C NMR shows many aromatic carbons, a carbonyl carbon (~166 ppm) and a methoxy carbon (~52 ppm). A reasonable fragmentation is:
- an aromatic phenyl fragment: c1ccccc1  
- a carbonyl/acid fragment: C(=O)O  
- a methoxy fragment: CO  

These fragments can be linked (e.g., as a methyl ester of a phenyl‑carboxylic acid) to give a molecule consistent with the formula C₁₁H₁₇O₇.  

All three SMILES strings are valid.</thought>
<final_answer>['c1ccccc1', 'C(=O)O', 'CO']</final_answer>
